raw_text:
Below is a structured 12-week postpartum return-to-training program designed for a 33-year-old client, 4 weeks post uncomplicated C-section, cleared for light activity only (walking, no abs, no heavy lifting) until 6-week check. Training is home-based with only a yoga mat. The plan emphasizes pelvic health, core reactivation with diastasis-safe progressions, gradual cardiovascular work, gentle strength work with proper bracing, and recovery. It progresses in phases with clear week-by-week guidance. Adjustments should be made if the client experiences pain, bleeding, or diastasis symptoms.

Important notes upfront
- Core/safety: Avoid high-load ab curls, crunches, traditional planks if she has diastasis recti concerns or if the six-week check hasn’t confirmed readiness. Emphasize pelvic floor engagement (bracing, diaphragmatic breathing) and gradual progressive loading of the core with diastasis-safe exercises.
- Pain signals: Any pelvic floor/pelvic girdle pain, urinary leakage, or increased diastasis should pause progression and seek clinician guidance.
- Signals of readiness: If cleared by OB at six weeks for light resistance, we will introduce light resistance and controlled core work in Week 7 onward, respecting her body.
- Equipment: Only a yoga mat is needed. Optional: resistance bands (light) and a small pillow or cushion for support.

Overall structure
- Frequency: 4 sessions per week (A, B, C, D) with at least one optional mobility session.
- Intensity: RPE 3-5/10 early weeks, gradually progressing to sustainable 6-7/10 as tolerated.
- Core focus: Throughout, with diastasis-safe activation cues. Strength work progresses with hips, glutes, quads, back, shoulders, and light core engagement.

Phase 0: Foundation and safety (Weeks 1–2)
Goal: Reconnect with diaphragmatic breathing, activate pelvic floor, establish gentle movement habits, begin low-load posterior chain and hip mobility.

Week 1
Session A
- Warm-up (5 minutes): diaphragmatic breathing (inhale 4, exhale 6), 8–10 breaths; gentle cat-cow on all fours (if comfortable), rocking pelvis.
- Pelvic floor and core activation (10 minutes):
  - BK contract: 3 sets x 5–8 reps of quick pelvic floor squeezes (hold 1–2 seconds).
  - Abdominal bracing with exhale to brace around the ribcage (do 3 sets x 5–6 reps, each 3–4 seconds, no crunch).
  - Pelvic tilts on back with knees bent, minimal spine movement: 2 sets x 10 reps.
- Hip and glute prep (8–10 minutes):
  - Glute bridges (no heavy loading): 2 sets x 12 reps, hold top 1–2 seconds.
  - Clam shells with a small pillow between knees if needed: 2 sets x 12 reps per side.
- Mobility (5 minutes): hip flexor and hamstring gentle stretch, no pain.
- Cool-down (5 minutes): gentle child’s pose, 4–6 slow diaphragmatic breaths.

Session B
- Warm-up (5 minutes): marching in place, shoulder rolls.
- Low-load full-body movements:
  - Modified dead bug (on back, arms/legs moving with breathing): 2–3 sets x 6–8 reps per side.
  - Standing hip hinge with light stance (no weight): 2 sets x 12–15 reps, focusing on hip hinge and glute engagement.
- Lower body activation:
  - Side-lying leg lifts (abductors): 2 sets x 12 reps per side.
  - Seated leg extension with light resistance band if available (no knee pain): 2 sets x 12 reps.
- Posture and breath work: scapular resets (2 sets x 10 slow squeezes).
- Cool-down (5 minutes): gentle forward fold, hips open.

Session C (optional mobility session)
- 20–25 minutes of gentle mobility and breath work:
  - Thoracic mobility with child’s pose reach.
  - Pelvic tilts, lower back mobility on the floor.
  - Ankle, hip, and shoulder circles.

Week 2
Goal: Increase awareness of diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor engagement in basic movements, and small increases in volume.

Session A
- Warm-up (5 minutes): diaphragmatic breathing with 8–10 breaths, 3 rounds; posture cues.
- Core activation progression:
  - Pelvic floor quick taps: 3 sets x 8 reps.
  - Quadruped diaphragmatic breathing (crawl position): 2–3 sets x 6 breaths per side, with abdomen relaxed on exhale.
- Hip and glute strengthening:
  - Glute bridges with a slower tempo (2 seconds up, 2 seconds down): 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Side-lying clams with a controlled tempo: 2 sets x 12 reps per side.
- Mobility and gluteal activation:
  - Supine knee to chest stretch, 30 seconds per leg.
- Cool-down: 5 minutes breathing and gentle hamstring stretch.

Session B
- Warm-up (5 minutes): march with thoracic extension.
- Lower body activation:
  - Standing hip hinge into small range (no weight): 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Bird-dog (kneeling or half-kour with knee down): 2–3 sets x 6 reps per side, focus on controlled breathing.
- Posture and upper body:
  - Seated row with resistance band (if available) or towel, 2 sets x 12 reps, keep shoulders down.
  - Wall scap push-ups (gentle): 2 sets x 8–10 reps.
- Core control drill: dead bug progression with breathing: 2–3 sets x 6–8 reps per side.
- Cool-down: 5 minutes.

Session C (Mobility/Morning movement)
- 15–20 minutes: light mobility, hip flexor release, thoracic extension on floor, neck mobility.

Week 3–4: Emphasis on building consistency, safe loading, and prep for light resistance
Goal: Add gentle resistance (breath-coordinated) and longer hold times while maintaining diastasis-safe cues.

Week 3
Session A
- Warm-up (5–7 minutes): diaphragmatic breathing with 6–8 breaths, then cat-cow.
- Core and rib-cage activation:
  - Diaphragmatic breathing with rib cage expansion (hands on ribs): 3 sets x 6 breaths.
  - Pelvic floor activation with abdominal bracing: 3 sets x 6–8 reps, 2–3 seconds hold.
- Lower body:
  - Glute bridges with 2–3 second hold at top: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Hip bridges assisted with a partner or strap if available (gentle): 2 sets x 10 reps.
- Mobility and posture: hip flexor stretch, hamstring stretch, 30 seconds each.

Session B
- Warm-up (5 minutes): marching, light arm circles.
- Core-friendly loading:
  - Mini deadlift with light object (water bottle): 2–3 sets x 12 reps, neutral spine.
  - Seated leg extension with light resistance band only if comfortable: 2 sets x 12 reps.
- Upper body activation:
  - Seated rows with resistance band: 2–3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Shoulder taps from a tall kneeling position, minimal spine twist: 2 sets x 8 reps per side.
- Core control:
  - Dead bug with extended leg, slow breathing: 2–3 sets x 6–8 reps per side.
- Cool-down: 5 minutes.

Week 4
Session A
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes breathing work.
- Core progression:
  - Modified hollow hold (neutral spine, small engagement, hold 5–8 seconds) with 2–3 reps.
  - Diaphragm-assisted pelvic floor activation sequence: 3 sets x 6 reps.
- Lower body (gentle resistance):
  - Sumo squat with light chair support (no depth beyond comfortable): 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Glute bridges with single-leg progression (supported): 2 sets x 8 reps per side.
- Mobility and recovery: hip openers, child’s pose 30–60 seconds.

Session B
- Warm-up: 5 minutes dynamic leg swings (gentle), ankle circles.
- Upper body:
  - Push-up progression against wall or countertop: 3 sets x 8–10 reps.
  - Bent-over row with light resistance band or towel: 2–3 sets x 12 reps.
- Core focus:
  - Side planks are not recommended yet. Instead, quadruped opposite arm/leg extension (bird-dog) with careful cueing: 2–3 sets x 6 reps per side.
- Cool-down: thoracic mobility, deep breathing.

Phase transition: Six-week check-in (Week 5) and readiness for light resistance
From Week 5 onward, if cleared for light resistance, we introduce progressive loading and more structured workouts while staying diastasis-safe.

Phase I: Foundations ofReturn to Training (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: Re-introduce gentle resistance and basic full-body workouts with a focus on technique, tempo, and pelvic health.

Week 5
Session A
- Warm-up (5–7 minutes): diaphragmatic breathing with 8–10 breaths.
- Core and pelvic floor:
  - Diaphragmatic breathing while performing a 5-second exhale through pursed lips to cue pelvic floor engagement.
  - Modified planks or prone isolations only if diastasis allows (avoid full front planks if high DR or discomfort). Consider a 5–8 second hold of a prone “plant” without loading the abdominal wall.
- Lower body strength:
  - Bodyweight squats (or chair-supported): 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Glute bridges with 2-second hold: 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Mobility and recovery: hip flexor and hamstring stretches.

Session B
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes light cardio (march in place) and arm circles.
- Upper body:
  - Push-ups from a wall or elevated surface: 3 sets x 8–12 reps.
  - Resistance band row or towel pull-aparts: 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Core and spine control:
  - Bird-dog: 3 sets x 8 reps per side.
- Cool-down: 5–7 minutes.

Week 6
Session A
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes dynamic movement.
- Lower body:
  - Goblet squat using light weight (water bottle or dumbbell if available) or two-arm kettlebell deadlift style with light load: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Glute bridge with single-leg progression (no loaded spine): 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps per side.
- Core:
  - Dead bug with band resistance: 3 sets x 8 reps per side.
- Mobility: hip opening sequence.

Session B
- Warm-up: 5 minutes cardio + mobility.
- Upper body:
  - Dumbbell-like (or resistance band) press from floor or incline: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Seated row with resistance band: 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Core:
  - Side-lying clams with resistance band if available: 2 sets x 12 reps per side.
- Cool-down: 5 minutes.

Week 7–8
These weeks introduce more structured resistance while staying mindful of diastasis.
Session A
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes.
- Full-body circuit (3 rounds, 45–60 seconds per exercise, 90 seconds rest between rounds):
  - Chair-supported split squat (gentle depth).
  - Glute bridge or hip thrust with light weight.
  - Push-up on elevated surface or from knees.
  - Row with resistance band.
  - Bird-dog or contralateral leg extension.
- Core: 2 sets of 6–8 reps of modified hollow holds or dead bugs if tolerable.
- Cool-down: 5–7 minutes.

Session B
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes.
- Compound emphasis:
  - Romanian deadlift with light weight or guided hinge movements: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Step-ups onto a low step or stable chair: 3 sets x 12 reps per leg.
  - Shoulder press with light resistance band or dumbbells: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Bent-over row: 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Core:
  - Pallof press with light band or hold at chest level: 3 sets x 8–10 reps per side.
- Cool-down: 5–7 minutes.

Phase II: Progressive Loading and Conditioning (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: Build strength and endurance with controlled progression; maintain diastasis-safe technique; incorporate more structured cardio.

Week 9
Session A
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes.
- Full-body strength circuit (4 rounds, 35–45 seconds work per exercise):
  - Goblet squat or sumo squat.
  - Hip thrusts with light load.
  - Dumbbell floor press or push-up with elevated knees.
  - One-arm row with resistance band.
- Core:
  - Dead bug with light abdominal bracing; 3 sets x 8–10 reps per side.
- Conditioning: 5–8 minutes of brisk walking or low-impact cardio.

Session B
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes.
- Lower body:
  - Walking lunges (controlled, limited depth) or static lunges: 3 sets x 10 reps per leg.
  - Glute bridges or hip thrusts: 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Upper body:
  - Seated or standing row: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Shoulder press with light resistance band: 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Core:
  - Pallof press: 3 sets x 10 reps per side.
- Cool-down: 5–7 minutes.

Week 10
Session A
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes.
- Strength:
  - Romanian deadlift with light/moderate weight: 3 sets x 8–10 reps.
  - Front or back squad progression: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Push-ups from knees or incline: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Inverted row under a sturdy table: 3 sets x 10–12 reps.
- Core:
  - Dead bug progressed (add light band): 3 sets x 8 reps per side.
- Conditioning: 8–12 minutes brisk walk or stationary bike if available.

Session B
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes.
- Full-body conditioning circuit (4 rounds):
  - Dumbbell or resistance band RDL to row combo: 12 reps.
  - Split squats with light load: 12 reps per leg.
  - Floor press or push-up: 12 reps.
  - Hip thrusts with band or light weight: 12 reps.
- Core:
  - Anti-rotation Pallof press: 3 sets x 10 reps per side.
- Cool-down: 5–7 minutes.

Week 11
- Emphasis on stability, mobility, and higher quality reps
Session A
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes.
- Strength:
  - Goblet squat with moderate weight: 3 sets x 10–12 reps.
  - Hip thrusts with moderate load: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Dumbbell shoulder press: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Seated row: 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Core:
  - Side plank progression not recommended; instead, anti-rotation with Pallof: 3 sets x 12 reps per side.
- Conditioning: 10 minutes of brisk walk or light cardio.

Session B
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes.
- Lower body:
  - Walking lunges or reverse lunges with light weight: 3 sets x 12 reps per leg.
  - Glute bridges: 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Upper body:
  - Push-ups (knee or incline): 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Bent-over row: 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Core:
  - Dead bug with controlled breathing: 3 sets x 8 reps per side.

Week 12
- Peak week for gradual progression and readiness check
Session A
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes.
- Full-body strength circuit (4 rounds):
  - Goblet squat: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Hip thrust: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Push-up: 3 sets x 12 reps.
  - Row: 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Core:
  - Anti-rotation Pallof: 3 sets x 12 reps per side.
- Conditioning: 12–15 minutes of steady-state cardio (fast-paced walk) or intervals if tolerated.

Session B
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes.
- Mobility and stability:
  - Hip hinge patterns, dead bug progressions, glute activation work.
- Conditioning: 15–20 minutes of cardio.

Nutrition and recovery guidance (throughout the 12 weeks)
- Caloric intake: Ensure energy availability for recovery and milk production if applicable. Avoid extreme restrictions; focus on a balanced, nutrient-dense intake.
- Protein: Aim for 1.0–1.2 g/kg body weight per day to support tissue repair and lean tissue preservation.
- Hydration: Target 2.3–3.7 liters per day (adjust for activity and climate) with water and electrolyte balance as needed.
- Meals around workouts: Include a protein source and some carbs within 1–2 hours after workouts to support recovery.
- Fiber and micronutrients: Emphasize vegetables, fruits, whole grains, lean proteins, healthy fats to support energy and recovery.
- Sleep and recovery: Prioritize sleep; aim for 7–9 hours when possible. Include 1–2 days of lighter activity or complete rest if fatigued.
- Pelvic health and diastasis considerations: If diastasis recti is present, avoid traditional crunches or high-load abdominal movements. Prefer breathing-focused core work, dead bugs, modified planks, side planks (as appropriate), and progressive loading of safe core bracing.

Progression cues and safety
- Sign of progression: Consistently able to complete sets with proper form and no pain or bleeding; diastasis symptoms stable or improving.
- If pain or bleeding occurs: Pause the progression, return to the previous week’s level, and consult healthcare provider if persistent.
- If six-week OB check is not cleared yet for light resistance: continue Weeks 1–4-5 with emphasis on technique and low-load core controls; postpone resistance progression until clearance.

Buys and optional equipment
- If available: light resistance bands (yellow/or light), one moderate dumbbell (2–8 kg depending on strength), a stability ball or pillow for hip thrusts if you have it.
- If not available: use bodyweight progressions, household items as light resistance.
